answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity with cost escalation: each agent identity locks a bond returned only after a long vesting horizon, and the bond required rises sharply with the count of new identities one operator creates in a short window. A sybil farm cannot just mint cheap keys; every fake persona carries real capital at risk and a slow release schedule, like an opal held as collateral rather than cash. As the tide of registrations swells, marginal cost spikes, so each extra identity buys less influence. Slashed bonds burn shared capital, making the attack unprofitable.
